The trajectory is promising, but the work currently lives entirely at the surface level — the form is described, not yet designed. ⚠️ Where to Pivot: The critical blind spot here is the junction between the organic bumpy surface and the pedestal base. In every one of the four views, this connection is either glossed over or left visually ambiguous — the two forms appear to simply coexist without a structural or material logic explaining how they meet. Additionally, the 'bumpy surface' is communicated only through silhouette; there is no internal surface articulation (cross-contour lines, shading, or section cuts) that would tell a viewer whether this surface is convex, concave, hollow, solid, soft, or rigid. Avoid the trap of letting clean linework substitute for resolved thinking. 🛠️ Next Step: For your next iteration, draw a single large-scale cross-section cut through the object at its widest point — show the interior profile of both the bumpy surface and the base as a filled or hatched section drawing. Label the wall thickness, the connection method between the two forms, and indicate one material for each component. This one exercise will force you to resolve the structural ambiguity that currently undermines the feasibility and elaboration of the concept.
